title: Websites Around the World Rush to Fix Security Flaw
summary:
A major cybersecurity threat sent people scrambling on Wednesday to protect websites around the world.

Cybersecurity means keeping computers, networks and information safe from people who try to break in. This time, the problem was a weakness, or vulnerability, involving PHP. PHP is a programming language, a set of instructions that millions of websites use to work.

The FBI and the National Security Agency warned that hackers could use the flaw to take control of websites. They said attackers might also be able to get at sensitive information stored on those sites.

To stay safe, officials rushed to install security patches. A patch is a small update that fixes a weakness in software, a bit like putting a new lock on a door. While the patches were being added, some government websites were temporarily taken offline. Others remained offline entirely.

Artificial intelligence played a part in finding the problem. The company OpenAI says its artificial intelligence models helped uncover the vulnerabilities.

Problems like this show why software updates matter. When companies discover a weakness, they release fixes so that hackers cannot use it. Website owners then need to install those fixes quickly. Ordinary computer users can help protect themselves in a similar way by keeping their devices and apps up to date.

Some websites were still offline after the scramble. The quick response by officials showed how seriously experts take threats to the websites that so many people rely on every day, including government websites.
why_it_matters: Millions of websites, including government services, depend on shared software, so a single flaw can put information at risk worldwide unless fixes are installed quickly.

keywords.explanation: Cybersecurity is the work of keeping computers, networks and information safe from attackers.
A vulnerability is a weak spot in software that attackers could use to break in.
A programming language is a set of words and rules people use to give instructions to computers.
Patches are small software updates that fix problems or close security holes.
Hackers, in this story, are people who break into computer systems without permission.
Sensitive information is private data, such as personal details, that should be kept secret.
